q: The top layer of soil, rich in organic material and dark brown in colour, is called the _____
e: The top layer of soil, rich in organic material and dark brown in colour, is called the top soil. Top soil is the idea that completes this fact. Bedrock would fill a different blank than top soil.

q: The subsoil is lighter in colour than top soil because it contains _____
e: The subsoil is lighter in colour than top soil because it contains less humus. Less humus is the idea that completes this fact. No minerals would fill a different blank than less humus.

q: Bedrock, or parent rock, contains _____
e: Bedrock, or parent rock, contains no organic matter. No organic matter is the idea that completes this fact. High humus content would fill a different blank than no organic matter.

q: The mineral matter in soil makes up approximately _____ of its composition.
e: The mineral matter in soil makes up approximately 45% of its composition. 45% is the idea that completes this fact. 5% would fill a different blank than 45%.

q: Organic matter in soil accounts for about _____ of its total composition.
e: Organic matter in soil accounts for about 5% of its total composition. 5% is the idea that completes this fact. 20% would fill a different blank than 5%.

q: Soil texture is determined by the relative proportion of sand, silt, and _____
e: Soil texture is determined by the relative proportion of sand, silt, and clay. Clay is the idea that completes this fact. Humus would fill a different blank than clay.

q: Clay particles feel _____ when wet.
e: Clay particles feel heavy and sticky when wet. Heavy and sticky is the idea that completes this fact. Smooth would fill a different blank than heavy and sticky.

q: Sand particles are _____ compared to silt and clay.
e: Sand particles are the biggest compared to silt and clay. The biggest is the idea that completes this fact. Intermediate in size would fill a different blank than the biggest.

q: A soil with 30% clay, 50% sand, and 20% silt is classified as _____
e: A soil with 30% clay, 50% sand, and 20% silt is classified as sandy clay loam. Sandy clay loam is the idea that completes this fact. Silty clay would fill a different blank than sandy clay loam.

q: The essential macro-nutrients obtained from soil include nitrogen, phosphorus, and _____
e: The essential macro-nutrients obtained from soil include nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Potassium is the idea that completes this fact. Calcium would fill a different blank than potassium.

q: Nitrogen is especially important for _____ growth in plants.
e: Nitrogen is especially important for leaf growth in plants. Leaf is the idea that completes this fact. Root would fill a different blank than leaf.

q: Phosphorus is particularly associated with the development of a strong _____ system.
e: Phosphorus is particularly associated with the development of a strong root system. Root is the idea that completes this fact. Leaf would fill a different blank than root.

q: Potassium plays a key role in the _____ balance in plants.
e: Potassium plays a key role in the water balance in plants. Water is the idea that completes this fact. Nutrient would fill a different blank than water.

q: Most plants grow best when the soil pH is between _____
e: Most plants grow best when the soil pH is between 5.5 and 7.0. 5.5 and 7.0 is the idea that completes this fact. 4.0 and 5.0 would fill a different blank than 5.5 and 7.0.

q: If soil is too acidic, it can be treated by adding _____
e: If soil is too acidic, it can be treated by adding lime. Lime is the idea that completes this fact. Fertilizer would fill a different blank than lime.

q: Alkaline soils (pH > 8.5) can be treated with _____
e: Alkaline soils (pH > 8.5) can be treated with gypsum. Gypsum is the idea that completes this fact. Lime would fill a different blank than gypsum.

q: Lead particulates from automobile exhausts settle on soil near _____
e: Lead particulates from automobile exhausts settle on soil near highways. Highways is the idea that completes this fact. Rivers would fill a different blank than highways.

q: Pesticides in soil undergo degradation through biodegradation, chemical degradation, and _____
e: Pesticides in soil undergo degradation through biodegradation, chemical degradation, and photochemical reactions. Photochemical reactions is the idea that completes this fact. Evaporation would fill a different blank than photochemical reactions.

q: Repeated or excessive use of the same fertiliser is a source of _____
e: Repeated or excessive use of the same fertiliser is a source of soil pollution. Soil pollution is the idea that completes this fact. Noise pollution would fill a different blank than soil pollution.

q: Soil filters water, provides nutrients to crops, and helps regulate the Earth’s _____
e: Soil filters water, provides nutrients to crops, and helps regulate the Earth’s temperature. Temperature is the idea that completes this fact. Rotation would fill a different blank than temperature.
